title: Large-$N$ Carrollian Thermodynamics from AdS Black-Hole Phase-Space Contractions
summary: We develop the boundary and celestial interpretation of finite Carrollian black-hole thermodynamics. The bulk input is the phase-space contraction of the time generator and Newton constant for which the extended AdS first law has a finite Carrollian limit. We show that this finite first-law line has a holographic interpretation as a double-scaled low-temperature, large-$N$ ensemble: the Carrollian temperature decreases while the effective number of boundary degrees of freedom grows, leaving the thermodynamic products in the first law finite. The large-$N$ dictionary is anchored by the standard $\mathrm{AdS}_5/\mathrm{CFT}_4$ normalization of adjoint degrees of freedom and by the Brown--Henneaux central charge in $\mathrm{AdS}_3/\mathrm{CFT}_2$. We construct the finite Carrollian Brown--York stress tensor on the contracted AdS boundary and show that its global energy charge is the finite bulk Hamiltonian. We then derive the boundary form of the first law in terms of the spatial volume and the holographic degree-of-freedom normalization. This identifies the Hawking--Page locus with the zero of the chemical potential conjugate to the count of degrees of freedom. The same charge is the global Carrollian supertranslation charge, so the finite first law is the thermal zero-mode sector of the Carrollian Ward identity. Finally, we construct the celestial conformal-primary representation of thermal Carrollian correlators. The finite celestial-basis correlators are rescaled double-scaled correlators obtained by combining the Fourier--Mellin transform with the rescaled thermal frequency window.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a finite Carrollian thermodynamics from black holes, showing it corresponds to a double-scaled low-temperature, large-N boundary ensemble, with a finite first law derived from the contracted AdS boundary via Brown-York stress tensor and celestial conformal-primary correlators.
AI.motivation: To understand the finite Carrollian limit of black-hole thermodynamics and establish its holographic interpretation as a double-scaled boundary ensemble where the Carrollian temperature decreases while effective boundary degrees of freedom grow, keeping thermodynamic products finite.
AI.method: The authors analyze the phase-space contraction of the time generator and Newton constant in the extended AdS first law to obtain a finite Carrollian limit. They construct a finite Carrollian Brown-York stress tensor on the contracted AdS boundary, derive boundary forms of the first law using spatial volume and holographic degree-of-freedom normalization, and build celestial conformal-primary representations of thermal Carrollian correlators via Fourier-Mellin transforms with rescaled thermal frequency windows.
AI.result: The finite first-law line holographically maps to a double-scaled low-temperature, large-N ensemble; the global energy charge of the finite Brown-York stress tensor equals the finite bulk Hamiltonian; the Hawking-Page locus corresponds to the zero of the chemical potential conjugate to degree-of-freedom count; and finite celestial-basis correlators emerge as rescaled double-scaled correlators.
AI.conclusion: Carrollian black-hole thermodynamics has a consistent finite boundary and celestial interpretation, linking the first law to thermal zero-mode sectors of Carrollian Ward identities and to celestial correlators.

title: De Sitter Representations
summary: We review the representations of so(1,D), the algebra of isometries of D dimensional de Sitter space. We cover the representations in all D, including mixed symmetry representations and fermionic representations, and connect them to the various types of fields that can propagate on de Sitter space. The presentation is from a physics point of view, favoring concrete constructions over abstract considerations.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews representations of the so(1,D) algebra (de Sitter isometries) across all dimensions D, covering mixed symmetry and fermionic representations, connecting them to fields propagating on de Sitter space from a physics-oriented perspective.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive physics-oriented review of so(1,D) representations relevant to de Sitter space, filling a gap for concrete constructions of mixed symmetry and fermionic representations across all dimensions.
AI.method: The authors adopt a physics-based approach favoring concrete constructions over abstract mathematical treatment, systematically covering representations in all dimensions D, including mixed symmetry and fermionic cases, and linking them to physical field types on de Sitter space.
AI.result: A thorough classification and explicit construction of so(1,D) representations, including mixed symmetry and fermionic ones, with clear connections to the corresponding field theories on de Sitter space across arbitrary dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The work offers a practical, accessible reference for physicists working on de Sitter space, bridging representation theory and field propagation in curved spacetime.

title: Conserved charges and $L_\infty$ algebras
summary: We give a formula for conserved charges in an arbitrary Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. The formula is expressed in terms of the theory's $L_\infty$ data alone, without reference to the derivative structure of the Lagrangian. Therefore conserved charges can be computed in nonlocal models, such as string field theory, where conventional methods break down. We also show that the formula correctly expresses the surface charge of general relativity in terms of the Brown-York stress tensor. Related computations in Yang-Mills theory suggest that spatial boundaries are dealt with in a natural fashion.

AI.tldr: The paper provides a formula for conserved charges in Lagrangian field theories using $L_\infty$ algebra data, enabling charge computation in nonlocal models like string field theory, and demonstrates its correctness for general relativity's surface charge and Yang-Mills theory.
AI.motivation: To derive a formula for conserved charges that works for nonlocal field theories (e.g., string field theory) where conventional derivative-based methods fail, by leveraging the algebraic structure of $L_\infty$ algebras.
AI.method: The conserved charge formula is expressed entirely in terms of the theory's $L_\infty$ algebra data, bypassing the need for the Lagrangian's derivative structure. The formula is tested on general relativity (recovering the Brown-York surface charge) and Yang-Mills theory.
AI.result: The $L_\infty$-based formula correctly reproduces the Brown-York stress tensor surface charge in general relativity and handles spatial boundaries naturally in Yang-Mills theory.
AI.conclusion: Conserved charges in arbitrary Lagrangian field theories can be computed solely from $L_\infty$ data, extending applicability to nonlocal theories and providing a unified, boundary-friendly formalism.

title: An observer's quantization of 3d de Sitter
summary: What is the density of states of the de Sitter static patch? We propose a definition and calculation of such a density in 3d dS. Our proposal involves a sum over an SL(2,$\mathbb{Z}$) set of Euclidean no-boundary Kerr-lens spacetimes sourced by a line-defect with given energy and spin - which in Lorentzian time represents an observer's worldline at the center of the dS static patch. We develop an exact quantum computation of the spectral density using a holographic duality between dS$_3$ gravity and two copies of $\mathbb{C}$LS, the complex Liouville string. The SL(2,$\mathbb{Z}$) Kerr-lens spacetimes map under the duality to an SL(2,$\mathbb{Z}$) family of generalized crosscap geometries. We compute the $\mathbb{C}$LS $\otimes$ $\mathbb{C}$LS crosscap amplitudes and show that they match the semi-classical gravity prediction. For the simplest non-trivial Kerr-lens space, the $\mathbb{C}$LS $\otimes$ $\mathbb{C}$LS description is, in turn, dual to two copies of the $GΣ$ effective field theory of the double scaled SYK model. The $GΣ\otimes GΣ$ theory lives on an observer's worldline in the static patch, setting the stage for developing a microscopic worldline hologram of 3d de Sitter.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a definition and exact quantum computation of the density of states in the 3D de Sitter static patch using a holographic duality between dS₃ gravity and two copies of the complex Liouville string (ℂLS), with contributions from an SL(2,ℤ) family of Euclidean no-boundary Kerr-lens spacetimes sourced by a line-defect representing an observer's worldline.
AI.motivation: To understand the quantum density of states of the de Sitter static patch, which is a fundamental open problem in de Sitter quantum gravity and holography.
AI.method: The spectral density is computed using a holographic duality between dS₃ gravity and two copies of the complex Liouville string (ℂLS ⊗ ℂLS). The computation involves a sum over an SL(2,ℤ) family of Euclidean no-boundary Kerr-lens spacetimes sourced by a line-defect. Under the duality, these map to SL(2,ℤ) generalized crosscap geometries. Crosscap amplitudes are computed exactly and shown to match semiclassical gravity predictions.
AI.result: The ℂLS ⊗ ℂLS crosscap amplitudes match the semiclassical gravity prediction. The simplest non-trivial Kerr-lens space is dual to two copies of the GΣ effective field theory of the double-scaled SYK model, living on an observer's worldline.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a microscopic worldline hologram of 3D de Sitter space, providing a foundation for understanding the quantum density of states and holography in de Sitter spacetime.

title: Magnetic monopole plasma oscillations and implications for TeV blazars
summary: Magnetic monopoles arise in many beyond Standard Model scenarios, symmetrize Maxwell's equations, and their existence would be tied to the quantization of electric charge. It has been argued that, when placed in an astrophysical magnetic field, monopoles can induce a magnetic version of plasma oscillations. In this work, we explore monopole-induced oscillations of the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF). We show that monopole-induced oscillations of the magnetic field lead to collimation of electrically charged particle trajectories, reducing the usual deflection by the magnetic field. The collimation effect impacts the deflection angle in the electromagnetic cascades of TeV blazars and leads to a decrease in the angular size of blazar secondary GeV halos. Therefore, the constraints on the secondary halo angular size from combined H.E.S.S. and Fermi-LAT observations translate into bounds on the magnetic monopole abundance. The bounds on the magnetic monopole flux obtained in this work from blazar 1ES 0229+200, depending on the IGMF strength, can be as strong as $F \lesssim 6 \times 10^{-23}\, \text{cm}^{-2} \text{s}^{-1} \text{str}^{-1}$ for low-mass monopoles $m \lesssim 10^6\, \text{GeV}$, stronger than existing laboratory and astrophysical bounds. The bound becomes subdominant to current constraints if the present-day IGMF value is stronger than $B \gtrsim 10^{-12}\, \text{G}$. At the same time, in the case of non-zero monopole abundance, the IGMF lower bound from TeV observations itself should be revised, resulting in a stronger lower bound at higher monopole number density.

AI.tldr: Magnetic monopoles can induce oscillations in the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF), which collimate charged particle trajectories and reduce deflection angles in TeV blazar cascades. This yields constraints on monopole flux as strong as F ≲ 6×10⁻²³ cm⁻² s⁻¹ str⁻¹ for low-mass monopoles (m ≲ 10⁶ GeV), surpassing existing bounds, while also revising IGMF lower bounds from TeV observations at non-zero monopole abundance.
AI.motivation: To explore whether magnetic monopoles, which appear in beyond Standard Model theories and would quantize electric charge, can induce magnetic plasma oscillations in astrophysical fields, and to determine if these effects produce observable signatures that can constrain monopole abundance.
AI.method: The authors analyze monopole-induced oscillations of the intergalactic magnetic field (IGMF) and show that such oscillations collimate electrically charged particle trajectories, reducing the usual magnetic deflection. They apply this to electromagnetic cascades from TeV blazars (specifically 1ES 0229+200) and translate combined H.E.S.S. and Fermi-LAT constraints on secondary GeV halo angular size into bounds on monopole flux.
AI.result: The monopole flux bound can be as strong as F ≲ 6×10⁻²³ cm⁻² s⁻¹ str⁻¹ for low-mass monopoles (m ≲ 10⁶ GeV), stronger than existing laboratory and astrophysical bounds. This bound becomes subdominant if IGMF B ≳ 10⁻¹² G. Conversely, at non-zero monopole abundance, the IGMF lower bound from TeV observations is revised upward.
AI.conclusion: Magnetic monopole-induced IGMF oscillations provide a new observable probe of monopole abundance via blazar secondary halo angular size measurements, yielding competitive constraints for low-mass monopoles and requiring revision of IGMF lower bounds in the presence of monopoles.

title: Charged and rotating near-horizon geometries in five dimensions
summary: We present new charged and rotating near-horizon geometries in five-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory in closed analytic form. The solutions can be parametrised by the charge and two independent angular momenta. We also generalise these near-horizon geometries to theories with an additional Chern-Simons term in the action multiplied by an arbitrary coupling constant. The new solutions have the same entropy relations as expected for charged versions of extremal Myers-Perry black holes and for rotating versions of extremal Reissner-Nordström-Tangherlini black holes, but they do not reduce to the Myers-Perry horizon in the vacuum limit. The horizon cross-sections are spherical and carry a Sasakian structure. We exploit this structure to prove a characterisation of our solutions: without any symmetry assumptions, they are the most general rotating extremal horizons for which the co-rotating electric field is a (non-zero) constant. We further extend this construction to higher dimensions, where we show that any Sasaki-Einstein manifold generates a two-parameter family of charged and rotating horizons.

AI.tldr: This paper presents new charged and rotating near-horizon geometries in 5D Einstein-Maxwell theory (with and without Chern-Simons term), characterized by two independent angular momenta and charge, with spherical Sasakian horizon cross-sections. It proves these are the most general rotating extremal horizons with constant co-rotating electric field, and extends the construction to higher dimensions using Sasaki-Einstein manifolds.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to construct explicit charged and rotating near-horizon geometries in higher-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory, as such solutions were previously missing in closed analytic form, and to characterize them via geometric structures (Sasakian/Sasaki-Einstein) without relying on symmetry assumptions.
AI.method: The authors derive new analytic solutions for near-horizon geometries in 5D Einstein-Maxwell theory parametrized by charge and two independent angular momenta, also generalizing to include a Chern-Simons term with arbitrary coupling constant. They exploit Sasakian geometry to prove a characterization theorem for these horizons and extend the construction to arbitrary odd dimensions using Sasaki-Einstein manifolds.
AI.result: New closed-form charged and rotating near-horizon solutions in 5D with two independent angular momenta; generalization to Chern-Simons theories; proof that these are the most general rotating extremal horizons with constant co-rotating electric field; extension to higher dimensions via Sasaki-Einstein manifolds yielding two-parameter families of charged rotating horizons.
AI.conclusion: The new solutions do not reduce to Myers-Perry horizons in the vacuum limit but match expected entropy relations for charged extremal Myers-Perry and rotating extremal Reissner-Nordström-Tangherlini black holes. The Sasakian/Sasaki-Einstein structure provides a natural geometric framework for classifying such extremal horizons.

title: Constraining Multiple Kinetically Mixed Dark Photons
summary: Extra U(1) gauge bosons under which Standard Model particles are uncharged, aka dark photons, are a simple and well-motivated extension of the Standard Model. There could be a single, but also several or even many such dark photons. However, most studies consider only a single dark photon. Here, we want to look at the more general case of multiple dark photons interacting with the Standard Model via kinetic mixing. We consider a range of standard probes, Cavendish experiments, light-shining-through-walls experiments, as well as energy loss in stars. To explore the rather high-dimensional parameter space of the masses and the kinetic mixing matrix, we pursue a statistical approach, considering different distributions for the kinetic mixing parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the scenario of multiple dark photons (extra U(1) gauge bosons) interacting with the Standard Model via kinetic mixing, extending beyond the typical single dark photon assumption. Using a statistical approach to handle the high-dimensional parameter space of masses and kinetic mixing matrices, the authors examine constraints from Cavendish experiments, light-shining-through-walls experiments, and stellar energy loss.
AI.motivation: Most existing studies focus on a single dark photon, but there could be multiple dark photons. This work aims to investigate the more general, realistic case of multiple dark photons interacting with the Standard Model via kinetic mixing.
AI.method: The authors apply a statistical approach to explore the high-dimensional parameter space of masses and kinetic mixing matrices, considering different distributions for the kinetic mixing parameters. They examine constraints from standard probes: Cavendish experiments, light-shining-through-walls experiments, and stellar energy loss.
AI.result: The paper derives constraints on multiple dark photon scenarios from various experimental and astrophysical probes.
AI.conclusion: Multiple dark photons are a well-motivated extension of the Standard Model, and a statistical approach is necessary to constrain the high-dimensional parameter space of masses and kinetic mixing matrices.

title: A Circle That Won't Return: The Fate of RR Fluxes and D-branes in Type 0A Tachyon Condensation
summary: We study the closed-string tachyon and doubled Ramond-Ramond sector of type 0A in light of the proposed M-theory description on $S^1\vee S^1$-the wedge of two circles joined at a point. In this picture the two RR copies are associated with the two circle components, which we call branches, and tachyon condensation corresponds to shrinking one branch to the type IIA endpoint. From the type 0A equations of motion, we derive the branch-balance condition for a tachyon stationary point and identify the branch-odd RR fluctuation that sources the tachyon around a symmetric background. We then analyze the fate of the collapsing branch RR data as one branch of the wedge collapses to the type IIA endpoint. For an isolated unscreened collapsing-branch $D_p^-$ source, a Gauss-law estimate shows that the long-range RR field-energy cost scales inversely with the shrinking circle and thus becoming infinitely costly, generalizing the $D0^-$-brane decoupling in the original wedge picture. We describe the infrared screening of the relative RR field through an effective higher-form Stückelberg mechanism and distinguish this from a possible discharge of localized relative charge. Finally, using standard Wess-Zumino couplings of D-branes, we identify an effective relative-charge carrier and derive a parametric thin-wall criterion for when such a discharge channel $D_p^- \to D_p^+$ can be energetically favored.

AI.tldr: This paper studies closed-string tachyon condensation and the doubled Ramond-Ramond (RR) sector of type 0A string theory in the M-theory description on $S^1\vee S^1$ (a wedge of two circles). It derives a branch-balance condition, identifies branch-odd RR fluctuations sourcing the tachyon, analyzes the fate of collapsing-branch RR data, and describes an effective Stückelberg mechanism for infrared screening. It also identifies effective relative-charge carriers and derives a thin-wall criterion for discharge channels like $D_p^- \to D_p^+$.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics of tachyon condensation and the role of the doubled RR sector in type 0A string theory within its M-theory description on a wedge geometry, and to explain how branch collapse leads to the type IIA endpoint while avoiding infinite energy costs from unscreened RR fields.
AI.method: The authors use type 0A equations of motion to derive the branch-balance condition, analyze Gauss-law estimates for RR field-energy costs, employ an effective higher-form Stückelberg mechanism for infrared screening, and utilize standard Wess-Zumino couplings of D-branes to identify charge carriers and derive parametric thin-wall criteria.
AI.result: The branch-balance condition for tachyon stationary points is derived. An unscreened collapsing-branch $D_p^-$ source incurs infinitely costly long-range RR field-energy (scaling inversely with the shrinking circle), generalizing $D0^-$ decoupling. Infrared screening via a Stückelberg mechanism is described, and a parametric thin-wall criterion for discharge channels $D_p^- \to D_p^+$ is obtained.
AI.conclusion: The work clarifies how tachyon condensation in type 0A leads to the type IIA endpoint, with branch collapse prevented from being energetically prohibitive by screening/discharge mechanisms, and identifies specific charge-carrier channels that can make such transitions favorable.

title: Axial-Vector Lattice Benchmarks Reveal a Common Medium Response of Meson Screening in Hot QCD
summary: Meson screening masses trace the dissolution of hadronic correlations in hot QCD. Combining lattice-QCD benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson--Schwinger baseline, we identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset and a finite-interval medium response. One axial-vector point fixes the response; remaining axial-vector data test it, and vector screening masses validate it without input. The framework predicts light-charm and bottom-containing spectra; its pseudoscalar--scalar extension gives conservative lower estimates for ordinary chiral partners.

AI.tldr: This paper uses lattice-QCD benchmarks and Dyson-Schwinger equations to study meson screening masses in hot QCD, identifying a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset and a finite-interval medium response. The framework is validated using axial-vector and vector screening masses, and predicts light-charm, bottom-containing spectra, and chiral partner bounds.
AI.motivation: To understand how hadronic correlations dissolve in hot QCD by studying meson screening masses, and to develop a framework that can predict spectra across different flavors and channels.
AI.method: Combining lattice-QCD benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson-Schwinger baseline, the authors identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset and a finite-interval medium response. One axial-vector point fixes the response; remaining axial-vector data test it, and vector screening masses validate it without input.
AI.result: The framework successfully predicts light-charm and bottom-containing spectra. The pseudoscalar-scalar extension provides conservative lower estimates for ordinary chiral partners.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework offers a validated approach to studying meson screening masses in hot QCD, with predictive power for various flavors and chiral partner relationships.

title: Dirichlet, Neumann, Mixed and self-dual holography: (self-dual) Yang--Mills theory II
summary: We consider Yang--Mills, Chalmers--Siegel and self-dual Yang--Mills (SDYM) theories within AdS/CFT correspondence. Bulk-to-bulk and boundary-to-bulk propagators are derived in various gauges and for Dirichlet, Neumann, mixed and self-dual boundary conditions. Three- and four-point holographic correlators are computed in the three theories to establish the relation between the observables thereof. This is a companion paper to [arXiv:2602.21658].

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes Yang-Mills, Chalmers-Siegel, and self-dual Yang-Mills theories within AdS/CFT correspondence, deriving propagators and computing holographic correlators to establish relations between observables across the three theories.
AI.motivation: To understand the relationships between Yang-Mills, Chalmers-Siegel, and self-dual Yang-Mills theories within the AdS/CFT framework, and to establish connections between their holographic observables.
AI.method: Derivation of bulk-to-bulk and boundary-to-bulk propagators in various gauges and boundary conditions (Dirichlet, Neumann, mixed, self-dual); computation of three- and four-point holographic correlators for all three theories.
AI.result: Established relations between observables of Yang-Mills, Chalmers-Siegel, and self-dual Yang-Mills theories through holographic correlators at three- and four-point level.
AI.conclusion: The three theories are related via their holographic correlators within AdS/CFT, with detailed propagator structures derived under multiple boundary conditions; this work serves as a companion to arXiv:2602.21658.

title: Double-real corrections to color singlet decay in a parton-shower inspired scheme
summary: We introduce a local infrared subtraction method for next-to-next-to-leading order QCD calculations in color singlet decays, with counterterms based on scalar radiators and pure splitting functions. Overlapping singularities in the multipole radiation pattern are disentangled by partial fractioning, and the kinematics mapping corresponds to iterated next-to-leading order kinematics. We verify that the double-real remainder to $e^+e^-\to\;q\bar{q}$ is rendered finite in the single and double unresolved limits and investigate the numerical convergence of the Monte-Carlo integral. We compute the phase-space integrals of the scalar counterterms in the back-to-back configuration, both analytically and with the help of numerical techniques based on sector decomposition.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a local infrared subtraction method for NNLO QCD calculations in color singlet decays, using scalar radiators and pure splitting functions with partial fractioning to handle overlapping singularities. It verifies the method's effectiveness for e+e- → qq̄ and demonstrates numerical convergence.
AI.motivation: To develop a local infrared subtraction method for next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD calculations in color singlet decays that effectively handles overlapping singularities in multipole radiation patterns.
AI.method: The method uses counterterms based on scalar radiators and pure splitting functions. Overlapping singularities are disentangled via partial fractioning. Kinematics mapping corresponds to iterated NLO kinematics. Phase-space integrals of scalar counterterms in back-to-back configuration are computed both analytically and numerically using sector decomposition.
AI.result: The double-real remainder to e+e- → qq̄ is rendered finite in both single and double unresolved limits. Numerical convergence of the Monte-Carlo integral is demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: The proposed subtraction method successfully handles NNLO QCD calculations for color singlet decays, with verified finiteness and numerical convergence in the e+e- → qq̄ test case.

title: Deformed BTZ Radiance and Single Trace $T\bar{T}$ Holography
summary: We generalize the "holar wind" mechanism proposed in arXiv:2303.00234 to the case of rotating $λ$-deformed BTZ black holes. These backgrounds, which interpolate between $AdS_3$ in the infrared and a linear dilaton spacetime in the ultraviolet, are realized as an exact $\frac{SL(2,\mathbb{R})_k\times U(1)}{U(1)}$ gauged-WZW worldsheet theory. The long string sector of the theory provides a holographic dual to single-trace $T\overline{T}$ deformed symmetric product $\mathcal{M}^p/S_p$ $CFT_2$ with a seed $\mathcal{M}$ carrying a central charge $c=6k$. By analyzing the geodesics and tunneling rates of probe particles and winding long strings, we show that the emission probabilities for both positive and negative deformation couplings are universally governed by the change in the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, $ΔS_{BH}$. A central result of our analysis is that the consistency of long string emission within the grand canonical ensemble dictates a unique value for the background B-field at the origin. We demonstrate that this thermodynamically fixed value matches precisely the prediction required for the string excitation spectrum to agree with the $\mathbb{Z}_w$ twisted sector of a single-trace $T\overline{T}$ deformed symmetric product orbifold. Finally, we sketch the extension of these results to a broader class of black holes whose long string sector is dual to single-trace $T\overline{T} + J\overline{T} + T\overline{J}$ deformed theories.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the "hole-um wind" mechanism to rotating λ-deformed BTZ black holes, showing that long string emission probabilities are governed by the change in Bekenstein-Hawking entropy (ΔS_BH). The authors fix the background B-field from thermodynamic consistency of the grand canonical ensemble, matching predictions for single-trace T\bar{T} deformed symmetric product orbifold CFTs, and sketch generalizations to T\bar{T} + J\bar{T} + T\bar{J} deformed theories.
AI.motivation: To generalize the "hole-um wind" emission mechanism from non-rotating to rotating λ-deformed BTZ black holes, and to establish thermodynamic consistency conditions that fix the background B-field, thereby strengthening the holographic duality between these black holes and single-trace T\bar{T} deformed CFTs.
AI.method: The paper uses an exact gauged-WZW worldsheet theory (SL(2,R)_k × U(1) / U(1)) to describe rotating λ-deformed BTZ black holes. It analyzes geodesics, tunneling rates of probe particles, and winding long strings to compute emission probabilities. Thermodynamic consistency of the grand canonical ensemble is used to fix the B-field at the origin.
AI.result: Emission probabilities for both positive and negative deformation couplings are universally governed by ΔS_BH. The thermodynamically fixed B-field matches the prediction required for the string excitation spectrum to agree with the Z_w twisted sector of a single-trace T\bar{T} deformed symmetric product orbifold.
AI.conclusion: The "hole-um wind" mechanism extends consistently to rotating λ-deformed BTZ black holes, with thermodynamic consistency fixing the B-field uniquely. The results also extend to broader classes of single-trace T\bar{T} + J\bar{T} + T\bar{J} deformed theories.

title: Supercool with PPO: Exploring Supercooled Phase Transitions via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions provide a powerful probe of hidden sectors and beyond the Standard Model physics. However, identifying phenomenologically relevant benchmark points remains computationally challenging, since viable and detectable signals typically occupy only a small fraction of the scanned parameter space. In this work, we introduce a reinforcement learning strategy based on Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to accelerate the search for gravitational wave signals from supercooled phase transitions in a minimal dark $U(1)_x$ sector. We construct a numerical reinforcement learning environment that maps the microscopic model parameters to the corresponding phase transition and gravitational wave observables, using a gauge-independent low-temperature formulation of the effective action. Several reward designs are developed to guide the agent toward parameter regions producing large gravitational wave amplitudes, broad frequency coverage, and detector sensitive benchmark points. We compare the PPO scans with conventional Monte Carlo scans in both narrow and broad windows of the $U(1)_x$ vacuum expectation value. Our results demonstrate that PPO provides an efficient goal-directed search strategy for gravitational wave phenomenology and offers a broadly applicable framework for learning-assisted exploration of high-dimensional scientific parameter spaces.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning strategy to efficiently search for gravitational wave signals from supercooled phase transitions in a minimal dark U(1)_x sector, demonstrating improved performance over conventional Monte Carlo scans.
AI.motivation: Identifying phenomenologically relevant benchmark points for gravitational waves from cosmological first-order phase transitions is computationally challenging because viable and detectable signals occupy only a small fraction of the scanned parameter space.
AI.method: The authors construct a numerical RL environment mapping microscopic model parameters to phase transition and gravitational wave observables using a gauge-independent low-temperature effective action, implement PPO with several reward designs targeting large wave amplitudes and broad frequency coverage, and compare with conventional Monte Carlo scans.
AI.result: PPO provides an efficient goal-directed search strategy for gravitational wave phenomenology, outperforming Monte Carlo scans in both narrow and broad windows of the U(1)_x vacuum expectation value.
AI.conclusion: The PPO-based reinforcement learning framework offers a broadly applicable method for learning-assisted exploration of high-dimensional scientific parameter spaces beyond gravitational wave phenomenology.

title: Duality-covariant particles and exotic branes
summary: In this paper we construct duality-covariant worldvolume dynamics of particles and branes. We extend known actions and phase space formulations to include the hidden $E_8$ symmetry of 11D supergravity, analogous to the Ehlers symmetry of 4D gravity. Making the worldvolume theory manifestly duality-covariant requires the ancillary structure of $E_8$ exceptional field theory to be taken into account. For zero-branes, we propose an enlarged worldline model with a coadjoint orbit term to encode this. More generally, we propose worldvolume theories for arbitrary exotic branes in a way that generalises the known gauged sigma model of the Kaluza-Klein monopole. These are natural in the duality-covariant Hamiltonian formulation employed here. We discuss the case of zero-branes in eleven dimensions as an illustrative example.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs duality-covariant worldvolume dynamics for particles and branes, extending known actions to include the hidden $E_8$ symmetry of 11D supergravity, using the framework of $E_8$ exceptional field theory. It proposes enlarged worldline models with coadjoint orbit terms for zero-branes and generalises gauged sigma models for exotic branes within a duality-covariant Hamiltonian formulation.
AI.motivation: To extend the worldvolume dynamics of particles and branes to incorporate the hidden $E_8$ duality symmetry of 11D supergravity (analogous to Ehlers symmetry in 4D gravity), making the theory manifestly duality-covariant.
AI.method: The authors employ a duality-covariant Hamiltonian formulation, using the ancillary structure of $E_8$ exceptional field theory. For zero-branes, an enlarged worldline model with a coadjoint orbit term is proposed. For exotic branes, the approach generalises the known gauged sigma model of the Kaluza-Klein monopole.
AI.result: Duality-covariant worldvolume theories for arbitrary exotic branes are proposed within the $E_8$ exceptional field theory framework, with explicit construction for zero-branes in eleven dimensions as an illustrative example.
AI.conclusion: The construction successfully extends the duality-covariant description of branes to include hidden exceptional symmetries, providing a unified framework via the Hamiltonian formulation and exceptional field theory.

title: Thermal Emission of Dark Photons from Earth's Core
summary: Dark photons in the sub-eV regime may be produced by the Earth's hot core, representing a much less extreme environment than stellar cores. We consider this possibility and estimate constraints on the kinetic mixing parameter $\varepsilon$ that governs dark photon coupling to charged particles, using Earth core cooling arguments, as well as dark matter direct detection bounds from SENSEI and DAMIC-M experiments. Our estimates suggest that the current results from these experiments constrain new dark photon parameter space. We also find that the proposed Oscura experiment may reach two to three orders of magnitude below existing bounds on $\varepsilon$, for dark photon masses $\sim 10^{-4}$ eV, depending on the assumed parameters characterizing the Earth core.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that sub-eV dark photons could be produced in Earth's hot core, and uses Earth cooling constraints alongside dark matter direct detection experiments (SENSEI, DAMIC-M, and future Oscura) to constrain the kinetic mixing parameter ε, finding new excluded parameter space and potential future sensitivity improvements of 2-3 orders of magnitude for masses around 10⁻⁴ eV.
AI.motivation: To explore a new production channel for sub-eV dark photons via Earth's hot core, which is a less extreme environment than stellar cores, and to derive competitive constraints using terrestrial observations and existing experiments.
AI.method: Dark photon production from Earth's hot core is modeled, and constraints are derived from Earth core cooling arguments and from direct detection bounds of SENSEI and DAMIC-M experiments. Future sensitivity projections are made for the proposed Oscura experiment.
AI.result: Current SENSEI and DAMIC-M data already constrain new dark photon parameter space. The future Oscura experiment could reach 2-3 orders of magnitude below existing bounds on ε for dark photon masses around 10⁻⁴ eV.
AI.conclusion: Earth's core provides a viable alternative production site for dark photons with competitive constraints; upcoming experiments will significantly expand sensitivity.

title: Holographic $s$- and $p$-wave superconductors from the $4D$ regularization of Einstein-Lovelock theory
summary: We investigate holographically dual descriptions of $(2+1)$-dimensional s-wave and p-wave superconductors in the framework of regularized four-dimensional Einstein-Lovelock gravity theories, incorporating higher curvature corrections beyond the Gauss-Bonnet sector. We first implement the 4D regularization of Einstein-Lovelock gravity with finely tuned coupling constants to include corrections up to any $K$th order in curvature. The bulk geometry is constructed from exact black-brane solutions characterized by the fine-tuned Lovelock coupling $α$ and the highest power of curvature in the Lagrangian K. We then analyze the condensation of scalar and vector operators dual to minimally coupled matter fields, focusing on two bulk-field mass prescriptions, which significantly affect the superconducting phase. Our results demonstrate that higher curvature terms significantly modify the phase structure of both s-wave and p-wave systems and enhance the sensitivity of the condensates and critical temperatures to the gravitational couplings. In both cases, the critical temperature generally increases with the maximal curvature order K, leading to higher-$T_c$ phases compared to Einstein gravity, particularly for negative $α$. The coupling $α$ effectively governs the strength of higher curvature interactions in the bulk: positive $α$ suppresses condensation and lowers $T_c$, whereas negative $α$ enhances superconducting order and promotes higher-$T_c$ phases relative to Einstein gravity. We further study the optical conductivity and find that both the gap frequency and the ratio $ω_g/T_c$ exhibit a strong dependence on $α$ and $K$, deviating from the universal Einstein-gravity result. Higher curvature effects enhance the superconducting gap scale. Notably, the p-wave system shows a stronger sensitivity to the mass-fixing prescription compared to the s-wave case.

AI.tldr: The paper studies holographic s-wave and p-wave superconductors in 4D regularized Einstein-Lovelock gravity with higher curvature corrections. Higher curvature terms significantly modify phase structures, with negative coupling α enhancing critical temperatures and positive α suppressing them. The gap frequency and ω_g/T_c ratio deviate from Einstein gravity results, with p-wave showing stronger sensitivity to mass prescriptions.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher curvature corrections beyond Gauss-Bonnet affect the holographic description of superconducting phases in (2+1)-dimensions, and to investigate deviations from standard Einstein gravity results for critical temperatures and optical conductivity.
AI.method: Regularization of 4D Einstein-Lovelock gravity with fine-tuned coupling constants up to Kth order in curvature; construction of exact black-brane solutions; analysis of scalar and vector operator condensation with two bulk-field mass prescriptions; computation of optical conductivity.
AI.result: Critical temperature increases with curvature order K, especially for negative α; positive α suppresses condensation while negative α enhances it; gap frequency and ω_g/T_c ratio depend strongly on α and K, deviating from universal Einstein gravity results; p-wave system is more sensitive to mass prescription than s-wave.
AI.conclusion: Higher curvature corrections significantly modify the holographic superconductor phase structure, enabling higher-T_c phases through tuning of Lovelock couplings, particularly negative α, and break the universality of the gap-to-critical-temperature ratio.

title: Kinetic freeze-out and diffusion dynamics in small-system asymmetric collisions at sqrt(sNN)=200 GeV in light of a generalized Fokker-Planck distribution
summary: A generalized Fokker-Planck solution is used to examine the transverse momentum ($p_{T}$) spectra of neutral pions generated in small-system asymmetric collisions, $p$-Al, $p$-Au, $d$-Au, and $^3$He-Au, at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV. This framework provides a cohesive explanation of particle production over a broad range of transverse momenta. We extract the energy scale governing the transition between a thermal and a hard regime, the effective temperature ($T$), and the exponents determining the high-momentum falloff from fits to PHENIX data. $T$ increases systematically with the collision centrality and colliding system size, ranging from about 0.33 GeV in peripheral $p$-Al collisions to 0.45 GeV in central $^3$He-Au collisions. This increase is correlated with the average number of participant nucleons, $<N_{part}>$, and the charged-particle pseudorapidity density, $<dN_{ch}/dη>$, indicating that larger and more central collisions create a denser, more strongly interacting medium that freezes out at a higher temperature. The acquired transition scale and power-law exponents follow consistent patterns across systems and centralities, revealing details about the sharpness of the transition from thermal to hard processes, and the relative strength of momentum-space diffusion versus drag. Interestingly, when the gold target dominates the collision geometry in the largest system ($^3$He-Au), the transition scale becomes nearly independent of centrality, signifying saturation of the diffusion process. Our findings demonstrate that the generalized Fokker-Planck solution is a sensitive probe of transport properties and non-extensive dynamics in the quark-gluon plasma produced even in small-system relativistic collisions, and it consistently describes pion spectra in this set of collisions.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a generalized Fokker-Planck solution to analyze neutral pion transverse momentum spectra in small-system asymmetric collisions (p-Al, p-Au, d-Au, ³He-Au) at √sNN=200 GeV. The effective temperature T increases with centrality and system size (0.33–0.45 GeV), correlated with Npart and dNch/dη. The transition scale and power-law exponents show consistent patterns, with saturation observed in ³He-Au collisions, demonstrating the framework's sensitivity to transport properties in small-system QGP.
AI.motivation: To understand particle production mechanisms and transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma in small-system asymmetric collisions, using a generalized Fokker-Planck framework to bridge thermal and hard regimes across a broad transverse momentum range.
AI.method: A generalized Fokker-Planck solution is applied to fit neutral pion pT spectra from PHENIX data across four asymmetric collision systems (p-Al, p-Au, d-Au, ³He-Au) at √sNN=200 GeV, extracting effective temperature T, transition energy scale, and power-law exponents.
AI.result: T increases systematically from ~0.33 GeV (peripheral p-Al) to ~0.45 GeV (central ³He-Au), correlated with Npart and dNch/dη. Consistent patterns in transition scale and power-law exponents across systems. In ³He-Au collisions, the transition scale becomes nearly centrality-independent, suggesting saturation of diffusion.
AI.conclusion: The generalized Fokker-Planck solution is a sensitive probe of transport properties and non-extensive dynamics in QGP produced even in small-system relativistic collisions, consistently describing pion spectra across these collision systems.

title: Central charges $C_J$ and $C_T$ in QED$_d$-GNY model and scalar QED$_d$
summary: We compute the leading-order $1/N$ corrections to the central charges $C_J$ and $C_T$ in the conformal QED$_d$-Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) model and the scalar QED$_d$ in $d$ dimensions. The scaling dimensions of the lowest adjoint bilinear scalars are obtained to order $O(1/N)$ for general $d$. In $d=3$, the $U(1)$ Abelian gauge theory possesses a topological $U(1)$ global symmetry, and we evaluate the central charge $C_J^{\text{top}}$ of the topological symmetry current to subleading order in the $1/N$ expansion. Our interest in these theories is primarily motivated by their potential connection to the $SO(5)$ symmetric deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP). We compare the large $N$ results for the central charges $C_J$ and $C_T$ with the conformal data of the $SO(5)$ DQCP obtained from fuzzy sphere and conformal bootstrap. The large $N$ predictions of the QED$_3$-GNY model are found to be in reasonable agreement with the nonperturbative estimates for the $SO(5)$ DQCP.

AI.tldr: This paper computes leading-order 1/N corrections to central charges C_J and C_T in conformal QED_d-GNY and scalar QED_d models, obtaining scaling dimensions of adjoint bilinear scalars to O(1/N). For d=3, it evaluates the topological central charge C_J^top to subleading order in 1/N. The large N results for C_J and C_T show reasonable agreement with nonperturbative estimates for the SO(5) DQCP from fuzzy sphere and bootstrap, supporting a potential connection.
AI.motivation: The study is primarily motivated by the potential connection between the QED_d-GNY/scalar QED_d models and the SO(5) symmetric deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP), a key concept in condensed matter physics describing transitions between different ordered phases.
AI.method: The authors use the 1/N expansion (large N) technique, computing leading-order 1/N corrections to central charges C_J and C_T in conformal QED_d-GNY and scalar QED_d models, and obtaining scaling dimensions of the lowest adjoint bilinear scalars to O(1/N) for general d. For d=3, they evaluate the topological U(1) symmetry central charge C_J^top to subleading order.
AI.result: Large N predictions of the QED_3-GNY model for central charges C_J and C_T are in reasonable agreement with nonperturbative estimates for the SO(5) DQCP obtained from fuzzy sphere simulations and conformal bootstrap calculations.
AI.conclusion: The results support the potential connection between the QED_3-GNY model and the SO(5) DQCP, as the large N calculations match nonperturbative conformal data reasonably well.

title: Flavor Alignment and Mass Hierarchy: Doing Everything Scotogenically
summary: Flavor alignment and mass hierarchy in quarks are shown to be achievable together in a renormalizable theory using the dark sector, while keeping only the one Higgs doublet of the standard model.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a renormalizable theory where quark flavor alignment and mass hierarchy are achieved through the dark sector, using only the standard model's single Higgs doublet.
AI.motivation: To resolve the flavor alignment and mass hierarchy problems in quarks without extending the Higgs sector beyond the standard model's one Higgs doublet.
AI.method: Introduces a dark sector to generate the observed quark flavor structure while maintaining renormalizability and minimality in the Higgs sector.
AI.result: Flavor alignment and mass hierarchy in quarks can be simultaneously realized with only one Higgs doublet, mediated by dark sector interactions.
AI.conclusion: The dark sector provides a viable mechanism to address quark flavor puzzles without requiring multiple Higgs doublets, preserving minimality and renormalizability.

title: Generating Special Triangulations with Transformers
comment: 21 pages, 11 figures. Contribution to the edited volume "Recent Progress in Computational String Geometry" (World Scientific), based on the BIRS-CMI workshop (26w5653)
summary: Triangulations, i.e., well-structured decompositions of geometric objects into triangle-like pieces, are central objects in many domains of mathematics and physics. In particular, fine, regular, and star triangulations (FRSTs) of 4D reflexive polytopes give rise to smooth Calabi-Yau threefolds, which are of significant interest in string theory. However, the high dimensionality and combinatorial complexity of triangulations make them particularly challenging to model with classical numerical methods or machine learning. In this work, we show that transformers, equipped with an appropriate encoding scheme, can be effectively trained to representatively generate new FRSTs across a range of polytope sizes. Moreover, these models can also self-improve through retraining on their own output. This opens the door to both concrete applications to the classification of Calabi-Yau manifolds and further research in physics, combinatorics and algebraic geometry.

AI.tldr: Transformers can generate fine, regular, and star triangulations (FRSTs) of 4D reflexive polytopes, enabling new approaches to classifying Calabi-Yau threefolds relevant to string theory.
AI.motivation: Triangulations, especially FRSTs of 4D reflexive polytopes, are crucial for constructing smooth Calabi-Yau threefolds in string theory, but their high dimensionality and combinatorial complexity make modeling with classical numerical methods or ML extremely challenging.
AI.method: Transformers with an appropriate encoding scheme are trained to representatively generate new FRSTs across various polytope sizes; models can also self-improve via retraining on their own generated outputs.
AI.result: Transformers can effectively generate new FRSTs across a range of polytope sizes, and the models exhibit self-improvement through retraining on self-generated data.
AI.conclusion: This approach opens doors to concrete applications in Calabi-Yau manifold classification and further research in physics, combinatorics, and algebraic geometry.

title: An Ultraviolet Finite Theory of Scalars
summary: We construct a theory of scalars that is free of short-distance infinities to all orders in perturbation theory. Loop divergences are neutralized by momentum-dependent interactions that are ghost free and polynomially bounded. The finite counterparts of the usual one-loop scalar self-energy and beta function are straightforwardly computed. In a variant of this model, the one-loop mass renormalization is zero due to an inversion that swaps the ultraviolet and the infrared.

AI.tldr: A theory of scalars with momentum-dependent interactions eliminates short-distance infinities to all orders, with finite one-loop self-energy and beta function; a variant achieves zero one-loop mass renormalization via UV-IR inversion.
AI.motivation: To construct a scalar field theory that is free from ultraviolet divergences in perturbation theory, addressing the long-standing problem of infinities in quantum field theory.
AI.method: Introduces momentum-dependent interactions that are ghost-free and polynomially bounded to neutralize loop divergences; a variant employs an inversion mechanism swapping UV and IR to eliminate mass renormalization.
AI.result: One-loop scalar self-energy and beta function are finite and straightforward to compute; in the variant, one-loop mass renormalization vanishes.
AI.conclusion: The proposed theory provides a finite, perturbatively consistent scalar field framework without short-distance infinities, with potential implications for renormalization and UV-complete models.

title: The Sharp Edges of Calabi-Yau Manifolds: Designing Symmetric Models for Ricci-flat Metrics
summary: Computing Ricci-flat metrics on Calabi-Yau manifolds is challenging since no closed-form solutions are known. However, these computations are needed in order to make physical predictions in heterotic string theory, such as the masses of quarks and Yukawa couplings. In this manuscript, we present an overview of relevant literature for learning about Calabi-Yau manifolds, as ML researchers often face a steep learning curve when entering the field. Furthermore, we survey the impact of the manifold's symmetries on machine learning approximations to these flat metrics. We also characterise the isometries of Ricci-flat metrics, a result frequently omitted or used without proof. Then, we address symmetry breaking in point sampling and introduce a novel formula for computing volume ratios on general CICY manifolds. We conclude by presenting a new symmetry-aware model built using graph neural networks that avoids pathological behaviour witnessed in some other models.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a survey of literature on Calabi-Yau manifolds for ML researchers, analyzes symmetries of Ricci-flat metrics, introduces a novel volume ratio formula for CICY manifolds, and proposes a symmetry-aware GNN model that avoids pathological behavior in approximating Ricci-flat metrics.
AI.motivation: Computing Ricci-flat metrics on Calabi-Yau manifolds is needed for physical predictions in heterotic string theory (e.g., quark masses, Yukawa couplings), but no closed-form solutions are known and ML researchers face a steep learning curve entering this field.
AI.method: The paper surveys relevant literature, characterizes isometries of Ricci-flat metrics with proofs, addresses symmetry breaking in point sampling, introduces a novel formula for computing volume ratios on general CICY manifolds, and builds a symmetry-aware model using graph neural networks.
AI.result: A symmetry-aware GNN model that avoids pathological behavior observed in other models, along with a novel volume ratio formula for CICY manifolds and a characterization of isometries of Ricci-flat metrics.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides an accessible overview of Calabi-Yau manifolds for ML researchers and demonstrates that incorporating manifold symmetries into neural network architectures (via GNNs) improves the approximation of Ricci-flat metrics while avoiding pathological behavior.

title: Unitarity Cuts, t-channel Divergences and the KLN Theorem for Unstable Particles
summary: Many phenomenological calculations involving massless or unstable particles suffer from divergences as mediating particles go on-shell. One way to deal with these divergences is via the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg (KLN) theorem, which guarantees that by summing over all physically-degenerate processes, the divergences cancel and inclusive observables remain finite. However, actually implementing this theorem in practice requires handling disconnected diagrams, ill-defined distributional objects, threshold behavior and subtle regulator dependence. In this work, we formulate practical prescriptions for dealing with some of these issues by studying the KLN cancellation in an illustrative model exhibiting a t-channel divergence. We demonstrate intricate cancellations across several regularization schemes, connect our results to the complex-analytic structure of the underlying amplitudes, and take steps towards constructing a finite, fixed-order, inclusive t-channel collider observable. This work highlights both the utility of the KLN theorem, and also the technical subtleties and open questions involved with applying it in practice.

AI.tldr: This paper develops practical methods for applying the KLN theorem to cancel divergences in t-channel processes, demonstrating cancellations across regularization schemes and linking results to complex analytic structure, while highlighting technical challenges in implementing the theorem.
AI.motivation: Phenomenological calculations involving massless or unstable particles suffer from divergences when mediating particles go on-shell. The KLN theorem guarantees divergence cancellation by summing over degenerate processes, but practical implementation faces challenges with disconnected diagrams, distributional objects, threshold behavior, and regulator dependence.
AI.method: The authors formulate practical prescriptions by studying KLN cancellation in an illustrative model with a t-channel divergence, examining intricate cancellations across multiple regularization schemes and connecting results to complex-analytic structure of underlying amplitudes.
AI.result: Demonstrated intricate cancellations across several regularization schemes, established connections to the complex-analytic structure of amplitudes, and made progress toward constructing a finite, fixed-order, inclusive t-channel collider observable.
AI.conclusion: The work highlights both the utility of the KLN theorem for canceling divergences and the technical subtleties and open questions that remain when applying it in practice.

title: Dyeing form factors as amplitudes
summary: The double copy of form factors has revealed a striking feature: poles that are spurious from the gauge-theory perspective become physical propagators in gravity. At the same time, form factors obey hidden factorization relations on the kinematics of these poles. We explain both phenomena by introducing a dyeing procedure, which promotes the color-singlet operator, or the Higgs particle representing it, to an adjoint massive state. The original form factor is recovered by the inverse bleaching operation, realized as a $U(1)$ decoupling of the dyed leg. In the dyed theory, these apparent spurious poles turn into ordinary physical propagators of colored amplitudes, and the hidden factorization relations follow from standard BCJ relations. Applying this framework to multiple operator insertions gives a systematic double-copy construction for multi-Higgs amplitudes and, as a byproduct, reveals scalar-ordering sectors. We also discuss higher-length scalar operators and fermionic operators, including the dyed vector construction for $\barψγ^μψ$, as well as a loop-level example.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a "dyeing procedure" that promotes color-singlet operators (like Higgs) to adjoint massive states, transforming spurious gauge-theory poles into physical propagators in gravity. The inverse "bleaching" recovers original form factors via U(1) decoupling. This framework systematically constructs double copies for multi-Higgs amplitudes, reveals scalar-ordering sectors, and extends to fermionic operators and loop-level examples.
AI.motivation: To explain two puzzling phenomena in the double copy of form factors: (1) spurious gauge-theory poles becoming physical propagators in gravity, and (2) hidden factorization relations obeyed by form factors on these poles.
AI.method: Introducing a "dyeing procedure" that promotes color-singlet operators (or their Higgs particle representatives) to adjoint massive states, then recovering original form factors via inverse "bleaching" (U(1) decoupling of the dyed leg).
AI.result: Spurious poles become ordinary physical propagators in the dyed theory; hidden factorization relations follow from standard BCJ relations. The framework systematically constructs double copies for multi-Higgs amplitudes, reveals scalar-ordering sectors, and extends to higher-length scalar operators, fermionic operators (including dyed vector construction for ¯ψγ^μ ψ), and loop-level examples.
AI.conclusion: The dyeing/bleaching procedure provides a systematic double-copy construction for multi-operator insertions, elucidating the origin of spurious poles and hidden factorization in form factor double copies.

title: Unified study of hyperon semileptonic decays in a relativistic three-quark model
summary: We present a unified theoretical study of semileptonic decays of ground-state octet hyperons using the relativistic three-quark model (R3QM). A key innovation of our approach is that all baryon wave functions are determined by fitting the baryon mass spectrum with a semirelativistic potential model, leading to predictions for weak transition amplitudes without free parameters. With the same wave functions, we calculate the branching fractions and lepton flavor universality ratios for the octet channels. The calculated values agree with the available experimental data and give predictions for channels with limited experimental information. We further compute the complete set of octet transition form factors without any additional free parameters, so that the weak current can be examined beyond the rate observables. In the well-measured $Λ\to p \ell^-\barν_\ell$ channel, the calculated leading vector and axial-vector form factors, $f_1(0)$ and $g_1(0)$, agree well with recent lattice QCD results, and the $g_1/f_1$ ratio is consistent with recent BESIII measurements. Beyond the leading vector and axial-vector terms, the complete form factor set separates the weak magnetism, second class, and the pole contribution associated with the partially conserved axial current (PCAC) relation. The weak magnetism term $f_2$ shows the clearest channel dependence compared with lattice QCD results, and its smaller values in some channels may point to transverse current strength not fully saturated by pure $qqq$ valence components. This work provides a framework for connecting octet hyperon weak form factors to the spin--flavor and spatial structure of baryons at the quark level, and gives testable weak current observables for future hyperon semileptonic decay measurements.

AI.tldr: A unified study of octet hyperon semileptonic decays using the relativistic three-quark model, with wave functions determined from baryon mass spectrum fitting, yielding parameter-free predictions for branching fractions, lepton flavor universality ratios, and complete form factor sets that agree with lattice QCD and BESIII data.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, parameter-free theoretical framework for semileptonic decays of ground-state octet hyperons, connecting weak transition amplitudes to the quark-level spin-flavor and spatial structure of baryons, and to produce testable predictions for channels with limited experimental data.
AI.method: Relativistic three-quark model (R3QM) with baryon wave functions determined by fitting the mass spectrum using a semirelativistic potential model, enabling parameter-free predictions of weak transition amplitudes, branching fractions, lepton flavor universality ratios, and complete octet transition form factors.
AI.result: Calculated values agree with experimental data; in Λ→p ℓ⁻ν̄ℓ, f₁(0) and g₁(0) match lattice QCD, and g₁/f₁ is consistent with BESIII. Weak magnetism term f₂ shows strongest channel dependence, with smaller values in some channels possibly indicating transverse current strength not fully saturated by pure valence qqq components.
AI.conclusion: The R3QM framework successfully connects octet hyperon weak form factors to quark-level baryon structure, provides testable weak current observables for future measurements, and suggests that pure valence qqq components may not fully capture the transverse current strength in certain decay channels.

title: Non-topological solitons in biadjoint scalar field theory
summary: Biadjoint scalar theory has been widely studied, due to its being closely related to the double copy correspondence linking gauge, gravity and related theories. In this paper, we continue a programme of work in elucidating non-linear solutions of this theory, and find a family of new solutions that are richer and more complex than previous cases. Using an ansatz that can be embedded in any choice of non-abelian colour groups, we demonstrate the existence of non-topological solitons, whose existence is protected by carrying a U(1) charge associated with certain rotations in colour space. The solutions are time-dependent, and closely related to the well-known Q-ball solutions in other scalar field theories. We also show explicitly that our solution set contains those that are stable under small perturbations within a consistent truncation of the theory, and have finite energy in addition to being localised.

AI.tldr: This paper discovers new, richer non-linear soliton solutions in biadjoint scalar theory that are time-dependent, carry U(1) charge via color-space rotations, and include stable, finite-energy, localized configurations analogous to Q-balls.
AI.motivation: To further elucidate non-linear solutions of biadjoint scalar theory, which is closely linked to the double copy correspondence between gauge and gravity theories, by finding solutions more complex than previously known cases.
AI.method: Using an ansatz embeddable in any non-abelian color group, the authors demonstrate non-topological solitons whose existence is protected by a U(1) charge from color-space rotations. Solutions are time-dependent, analogous to Q-balls, and analyzed within a consistent truncation for stability and energy localization.
AI.result: A family of new, richer non-linear solutions is found; these solitons are time-dependent, carry U(1) charge, and some are stable under small perturbations with finite energy and localization.
AI.conclusion: Biadjoint scalar theory supports Q-ball-like solitons with stable, localized, finite-energy configurations, expanding the solution space relevant to the double copy correspondence.

title: Holographic light-quark energy loss in a spinning plasma
summary: In this work, we investigate light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled plasma described by a spinning black-brane background obtained from the large-black-hole limit of the Myers--Perry geometry. The parameter $a$ characterizes the boost/rotation of the dual fluid in this holographic setup and is related to the angular velocity in the corresponding limit. We employ two complementary probes, the falling-string and shooting-string descriptions, to compute the stopping distance and the instantaneous energy loss of a light quark moving either transverse or parallel to the rotation axis. We find that increasing the temperature or the parameter $a$ reduces the stopping distance and enhances the instantaneous energy loss. The effect of $a$ is more pronounced for transverse motion than for motion along the rotation axis, indicating an anisotropic energy-loss pattern induced by the spinning/boosted background. These results are consistent with earlier holographic studies of jet quenching and heavy-quark dynamics in rotating plasmas.

AI.tldr: This paper studies light-quark energy loss in a strongly coupled, spinning plasma using holographic methods (falling-string and shooting-string) in a Myers-Perry black-brane background. It finds that increasing temperature or the rotation parameter $a$ reduces stopping distance and enhances energy loss, with anisotropy: transverse motion to the rotation axis experiences stronger effects than parallel motion.
AI.motivation: To understand light-quark energy loss in a rotating/boosted strongly coupled plasma, which is relevant for heavy-ion collision phenomenology where the quark-gluon plasma has non-zero angular momentum.
AI.method: The authors use holographic duality (AdS/CFT) with a spinning black-brane background derived from the large-black-hole limit of Myers-Perry geometry. They employ two complementary string-theory probes: the falling-string description and the shooting-string description, to compute stopping distance and instantaneous energy loss for light quarks moving transverse to or parallel to the rotation axis.
AI.result: Both increasing temperature and increasing the rotation/boost parameter $a$ reduce the stopping distance and increase instantaneous energy loss. The effect of $a$ is stronger for transverse motion than for motion along the rotation axis, revealing anisotropic energy loss. These findings agree with prior holographic studies of jet quenching and heavy-quark dynamics in rotating plasmas.
AI.conclusion: The spinning/boosted nature of the plasma induces anisotropic energy loss for light quarks, consistent with the broader holographic understanding of jet quenching in rotating strongly coupled plasmas.

title: Index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string and its decoupling limit
summary: Boruch, Emparan, Iliesiu, and Murthy recently discussed index saddles for 5d black strings, showing that the black string saddle admits a decoupling limit to a complex, finite-temperature BTZ \times S^2 saddle that computes the index of the dual CFT. In this paper, we pursue an analogous construction for the D1-D5-P black string. We construct a four-charge index saddle in the four-dimensional STU model as the BPS limit of the non-extremal four-charge black hole, and show that it exhibits the new form of attraction. We then uplift it successively to five and six dimensions, via the 4D-5D connection and a chain of string dualities, to obtain the gravitational index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string. We take a systematic decoupling limit of this index saddle and obtain the BTZ \times S^3 saddle that computes the index of the D1-D5 CFT.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs a gravitational index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string by starting from a four-charge index saddle in the 4D STU model, uplifting it to higher dimensions via dualities, and then taking a decoupling limit to obtain a BTZ × S^3 saddle that computes the index of the D1-D5 CFT.
AI.motivation: To extend the index saddle construction of Boruch et al. for 5d black strings to the D1-D5-P black string, and to show that a decoupling limit yields a complex BTZ × S^3 saddle that computes the CFT index.
AI.method: Start from a four-charge index saddle in the 4D STU model as the BPS limit of a non-extremal black hole, uplift to 5D and 6D via the 4D-5D connection and string dualities, then take a systematic decoupling limit to obtain the BTZ × S^3 saddle.
AI.result: Successfully constructs the gravitational index saddle for the D1-D5-P black string and obtains the BTZ × S^3 saddle that computes the index of the D1-D5 CFT.
AI.conclusion: The construction demonstrates an analogous index saddle decoupling limit for the D1-D5-P black string, generalizing the previous work on 5d black strings.

title: Torsional four-fermion interaction for Majorana neutrinos
summary: Fermions generate spacetime torsion, which can be eliminated, leaving behind an effective four-fermion interaction. This term will contribute an effective mass for neutrinos propagating through matter, similar to the Wolfenstein term coming from electroweak interactions. When the neutrinos are Majorana fermions and become massive via the Type I SeeSaw mechanism, there can be additional effects due to sterile neutrinos interacting with all fermions via the torsion-induced term, as well as due to the presence of new mixing parameters. We consider different scenarios with one sterile and one or two active neutrinos -- when the torsional interaction is diagonal in the mass basis and when it is not -- and analytically find these modifications. The T violation in the 2+1 scenario is discussed for some specific mixing between the torsion fields and the mass fields.

AI.tldr: Fermions generate spacetime torsion that leads to an effective four-fermion interaction, contributing to neutrino mass in matter, with additional effects from sterile neutrinos and mixing in Majorana/SeeSaw scenarios.
AI.motivation: To study how torsion-induced four-fermion interactions affect neutrino propagation in matter, particularly for Majorana neutrinos with sterile states via the Type I SeeSaw mechanism.
AI.method: Analytical derivation in 2+1 scenarios (one sterile + one/two active neutrinos), considering diagonal and non-diagonal torsional interactions in the mass basis, and analyzing T violation with specific mixing between torsion and mass fields.
AI.result: Torsion generates an effective mass term for neutrinos in matter analogous to the Wolfenstein term; sterile neutrinos acquire additional interactions via torsion; new mixing parameters emerge; T violation modifications are found in the 2+1 scenario.
AI.conclusion: Torsion-induced four-fermion interactions provide a gravitational contribution to neutrino effective masses in matter, with observable consequences for sterile-active neutrino mixing and CP/T violation.

title: Approximating Feynman integrals using complete monotonicity and Stieltjes properties
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, presented at Loops and Legs 2026
summary: We present two novel approaches for the numerical evaluation of Feynman integrals based on their universal analytic properties related to positivity, namely complete monotonicity (CM) and Stieltjes properties. Building on recent results, we exploit the fact that scalar Feynman integrals in the Euclidean region are completely monotonic functions, meaning that all their derivatives have a fixed sign. Building on this observation, the CM bootstrap allows one to reconstruct integrals from differential equations without explicit boundary data, yielding rigorous bounds. The second method is based on a refinement of CM. We prove that Feynman integrals, within a certain range of parameters, are not only CM but in fact Stieltjes functions. This enables the use of Padé approximants with provable convergence properties in the cut complex plane, providing an efficient method for analytic continuation and fast numerical evaluation. We illustrate the method with simple examples such as the massive bubble integral and discuss applications to multi-loop integrals, including the 20-loop banana integral. Finally, we comment on a number of extensions of these novel avenues for computing Feynman integrals.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces two new methods for numerically evaluating Feynman integrals using complete monotonicity (CM) and Stieltjes properties: a CM bootstrap that reconstructs integrals from differential equations without boundary data, and a Padé approximant method leveraging Stieltjes function properties for analytic continuation. Examples include the massive bubble and 20-loop banana integrals.
AI.motivation: To develop numerical evaluation methods for Feynman integrals that leverage their universal analytic positivity properties (complete monotonicity and Stieltjes), avoiding the need for explicit boundary data while providing rigorous bounds and provable convergence.
AI.method: (1) CM bootstrap: reconstructs Feynman integrals from differential equations without explicit boundary data, yielding rigorous bounds by exploiting complete monotonicity (all derivatives have fixed sign in the Euclidean region). (2) Padé approximants for Stieltjes functions: proves that Feynman integrals within certain parameter ranges are Stieltjes functions, enabling Padé approximants with provable convergence in the cut complex plane for efficient analytic continuation.
AI.result: Demonstrated effectiveness on simple examples (massive bubble integral) and multi-loop integrals including the 20-loop banana integral. The methods provide rigorous bounds and fast numerical evaluation with provable convergence properties.
AI.conclusion: The CM bootstrap and Stieltjes-based Padé methods offer novel, mathematically rigorous avenues for computing Feynman integrals numerically, with potential extensions to broader classes of integrals in quantum field theory.

title: CHESS: CHEbyshev pSeudo-Spectral transport for Feynman integral differential equations
summary: We present CHESS (CHEbyshev pSeudo Spectrum), a Wolfram Language package for high-precision one-dimensional transport of ε-factorized differential equations for Feynman master integrals. The solver works with the matrix obtained by pulling a differential one-form to a chosen path. This matrix may be supplied directly, or assembled from constant matrices and precomputed scalar pullbacks of the one-forms. The program combines Chebyshev-Lobatto spectral collocation, sparse matrix assembly, sequential propagation in the ε-expansion, and residue-based regularization of spurious regular singular endpoints. Benchmarks for large multi-scale integral families show rapid node convergence and agreement with independent reference data where such data are available. In the fixed local-series comparison used here, the Chebyshev transports also give shorter wall times; the reported process-tree memory usage is comparable for the smaller parallel runs and lower for the largest benchmark system in that comparison.

AI.tldr: CHESS is a Wolfram Language package that uses Chebyshev spectral collocation for high-precision numerical evaluation of Feynman master integrals via ε-factorized differential equations, showing fast convergence and competitive performance against fixed local-series methods.
AI.motivation: To provide a high-precision, efficient method for solving ε-factorized differential equations for Feynman master integrals, which are essential for multi-loop scattering amplitude calculations in perturbative QFT.
AI.method: Combines Chebyshev-Lobatto spectral collocation, sparse matrix assembly, sequential propagation in ε-expansion, and residue-based regularization of spurious regular singular endpoints. The differential one-form is pulled to a chosen path; the matrix can be supplied directly or assembled from constant matrices and precomputed scalar pullbacks.
AI.result: Rapid node convergence for large multi-scale integral families; shorter wall times compared to fixed local-series methods; comparable or lower process-tree memory usage for the largest benchmark systems.
AI.conclusion: CHESS provides a robust and efficient Chebyshev-based transport method for high-precision evaluation of Feynman master integrals, outperforming traditional fixed-series approaches in speed and scalability.

title: The gauge invariance of non-perturbative vertex prescriptions
summary: We study the gauge invariance of different continuum methods to include non-perturbative effects in gauge theories. We work with three dimensional quantum electrodynamics and implement vertices using two different methods: a set of coupled Schwinger-Dyson (SD) integral equations, and the self-consistent equations obtained from the 3-particle irreducible (3PI) effective action.
