We work in Landau gauge and assess the extent to which results are gauge invariant by checking how well the Ward identity is satisfied. Our results show that there is a fairly significant violation of the Ward identity at large coupling, although the 3PI effective theory is slightly better than the SD vertex. We also compare the results of both calculations with the commonly used Ball-Chiu ansatz and show that the agreement of the ansatz with both non-perturbative vertices is fairly good at small coupling but deviates more significantly at large coupling. We compare results for the two point functions of the theory and discuss the possible implications for phase transitions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies gauge invariance in 3D quantum electrodynamics by comparing Schwinger-Dyson equations and 3PI effective action methods, finding significant Ward identity violations at large coupling, with 3PI performing slightly better than SD, and the Ball-Chiu ansatz deviating significantly at strong coupling.
AI.motivation: To assess the gauge invariance of different non-perturbative continuum methods (SD equations vs. 3PI effective action) in gauge theories by checking how well the Ward identity is satisfied.
AI.method: Work in Landau gauge of 3D quantum electrodynamics, implement vertices using coupled Schwinger-Dyson integral equations and self-consistent equations from the 3-particle irreducible effective action, then compare results with the Ball-Chiu ansatz.
AI.result: Significant Ward identity violation at large coupling; 3PI effective theory is slightly better than SD vertex; Ball-Chiu ansatz agrees well at small coupling but deviates significantly at large coupling.
AI.conclusion: Neither method is fully gauge invariant at strong coupling; results suggest implications for phase transitions in gauge theories.

title: RG Running of Multiple Neutrino Mixing Parameters at Oscillation Experiments
summary: If the new physics scale is within the energy scale of neutrino oscillation experiments, it may lead to a renormalization group (RG) running effect between the production and detection processes as well as between different experiments. It is then possible to use multiple neutrino oscillation experiments to disentangle the multiple RG running parameters. We investigate this effect in a general model-independent sense for a variety of flavor structures in the context of upcoming experiments DUNE-ND, JUNO-TAO, and FASER$ν$2 that span a large range in neutrino energies and many different flavor combinations. We find strong sensitivity to the running effects of new physics with combination of these experiments, especially the possibility of addressing the non-trivial degeneracies.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the renormalization group (RG) running effect of new physics at energy scales accessible to neutrino oscillation experiments can be probed using multiple experiments (DUNE-ND, JUNO-TAO, FASERν2). The combination of these experiments, which cover a wide range of energies and flavor combinations, shows strong sensitivity to RG running effects and can resolve degeneracies in new physics parameters.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that multiple neutrino oscillation experiments spanning different energy scales and flavor combinations can be used to disentangle multiple renormalization group running parameters arising from new physics within the energy range of these experiments.
AI.method: A model-independent analysis of RG running effects from new physics in neutrino oscillations, using upcoming experiments DUNE-ND, JUNO-TAO, and FASERν2, which collectively cover a broad range of neutrino energies and flavor combinations. The study investigates sensitivity to RG running parameters and addresses degeneracies among them.
AI.result: Strong sensitivity to RG running effects from new physics is found when combining these experiments, particularly in resolving non-trivial degeneracies among multiple running parameters.
AI.conclusion: The combination of neutrino oscillation experiments with widely different energy scales and flavor compositions provides a powerful tool to probe and disentangle RG running effects from new physics.

title: Causality and the Equivalence Principle for Higher Energy Scattering
summary: Recently, it was proposed that the leading high-energy behavior of scattering amplitudes is universal, independent of charge, thereby extending the equivalence principle beyond the graviton pole. In this Letter, we derive a sharper causality constraint on such behavior by studying the Regge limit of colored scattering. Parameterizing a trajectory by $s^{α(t)}$ with $α(0)=2-δ$, we analyze the Shapiro/Wigner--Smith time-delays in the irreducible scattering channels. We show that any non-singlet trajectory with $δ< 1/2$ produces a growing sign-indefinite time-delay (with $δ=1/2$ a marginal, dimension-dependent case), which becomes dominant in the Regge diffusion region in the weak-gravity regime. The essential point is that, while the eikonal phase is naturally organized in $t$-channel irreducible representations, the physical time-delays are its eigenvalues in the $s$-channel. A non-singlet exchange therefore recouples into the physical channels with both signs, inevitably producing a negative time-delay in at least one channel.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a causality constraint (δ < 1/2 for non-singlet trajectories) on the Regge behavior of colored scattering amplitudes by analyzing time-delays in irreducible channels, showing that softer non-singlet exchanges inevitably produce negative time-delays due to recoupling between t-channel representations and s-channel physical channels.
AI.motivation: To extend the equivalence principle beyond the graviton pole and derive a sharper causality constraint on the universal high-energy behavior of scattering amplitudes, using Regge limit analysis of colored scattering.
AI.method: The study parameterizes Regge trajectories as s^{α(t)} with α(0)=2-δ, analyzes Shapiro/Wigner-Smith time-delays in irreducible scattering channels, and examines the recoupling between t-channel irreducible representations and s-channel physical channels in the Regge diffusion region under weak gravity.
AI.result: Any non-singlet trajectory with δ < 1/2 produces a growing sign-indefinite time-delay, with δ = 1/2 being a marginal, dimension-dependent case. Non-singlet exchanges recouple into physical channels with both signs, inevitably producing negative time-delay in at least one channel.
AI.conclusion: Causality imposes a sharper bound (δ < 1/2) on non-singlet Regge trajectories, derived from the sign-indefinite time-delay structure arising from the mismatch between t-channel irreducible representation organization and s-channel physical time-delay eigenvalues.

title: Coherent collective response in many-qubit systems for dark matter detection
summary: We propose an array of the Ramsey-type interferometers using $N$ superposition states, $(|0\rangle+ |1\rangle)^{\otimes N}$, as a sensor to detect wave-like dark matter. After the exposure to the dark matter wave, which induces the coherent qubit transitions, the signal is the imbalance between the probabilities of detecting 0 and 1. The signal-to-noise ratio in this scheme is proportional to $\sqrt{N} α$, where $α$ is the coupling of dark matter to the qubits, and thus the sensitivity to the coupling scales as $δα\sim 1 / \sqrt{N}$. For comparison, in the detection scheme based on the Rabi-type transition, $|0\rangle \to |1\rangle$, this scaling is achieved only when highly entangled $N$ qubits are used. Since the Ramsey-type measurement does not require entangled states, one can consider much larger $N$ by simply placing a large number of qubits within the de Broglie wavelength of the dark matter. We demonstrate that, using trapped-ion qubits in a linear Paul trap as the sensor, the projected sensitivity to the coupling matches or surpasses existing laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological bounds for $N \gtrsim 10^6$. We also evaluate its sensitivity to high-frequency gravitational waves. Our general framework should, in principle, be useful for other quantum sensing platforms.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Ramsey-type interferometer using N superposition states (instead of entangled states) to detect wave-like dark matter, achieving sensitivity scaling of 1/√N without requiring entanglement, and demonstrating with trapped-ion qubits that a sensitivity matching or surpassing existing bounds is possible with N ≳ 10⁶.
AI.motivation: To develop a more scalable and practical quantum sensing scheme for detecting wave-like dark matter that does not require highly entangled states, which are difficult to prepare and maintain for large N.
AI.method: The scheme uses N superposition states (|0⟩+|1⟩)^⊗N as a sensor in a Ramsey-type interferometer. Dark matter induces coherent qubit transitions, and the signal is the probability imbalance between detecting 0 and 1. The approach is contrasted with Rabi-type detection which requires entanglement. The method is analyzed using trapped-ion qubits in a linear Paul trap as a concrete platform.
AI.result: The signal-to-noise ratio scales as √N α, leading to a coupling sensitivity δα ∼ 1/√N. With trapped-ion qubits, projected sensitivity matches or surpasses existing laboratory, astrophysical, and cosmological bounds for N ≳ 10⁶. The framework also applies to high-frequency gravitational wave detection.
AI.conclusion: The Ramsey-type interferometer offers a practical, entanglement-free approach to quantum sensing of dark matter with sensitivity scaling favorably with N, and is applicable to other quantum sensing platforms and signals like gravitational waves.

title: Characteristic Lightcone Sources in SO(1,3) Yang-Mills Theory
summary: The SO(1,3)-symmetric reduction of Yang-Mills theory on Minkowski space yields a stress-energy tensor that is smooth on the timelike and spacelike Lorentz orbits but diverges on the lightcone that separates the two regions. We ask what consistent source this singularity represents. A natural cure is a real shift of the singular denominator. This does not regularize the source but instead moves the singular support onto a hyperboloid off the cone, where the corresponding source cannot remain both conserved and traceless. Our analysis shows that the displaced support cannot retain both properties, whereas a completion on the lightcone can. The matching condition fixes this completion up to one parameter $χ$, which has a causal interpretation as the relative weight of the future and past cones. On regular constant-time slices, the completed source carries zero total four-momentum, so its physical content is a residual causal charge inferred from its curvature response.

AI.tldr: The SO(1,3)-symmetric reduction of Yang-Mills theory produces a stress-energy tensor that is smooth except on the lightcone where it diverges. A real shift of the singular denominator fails to regularize the singularity properly, whereas a completion on the lightcone can preserve conservation and tracelessness. The completion is fixed up to one parameter χ representing the relative weight of future and past cones, and yields zero total four-momentum on constant-time slices, leaving only a residual causal charge.
AI.motivation: To understand what consistent source corresponds to the lightcone divergence in the SO(1,3)-symmetric reduction of Yang-Mills stress-energy tensor, and to find a regularization that respects both conservation and tracelessness.
AI.method: The paper examines a real shift of the singular denominator (which moves singular support off the cone) and contrasts it with a completion on the lightcone. Matching conditions fix the completion up to a parameter χ, interpreted as the relative causal weight of future and past lightcones.
AI.result: A real shift of the singular denominator fails to keep the source both conserved and traceless; only a lightcone completion satisfies both properties. The completed source has zero total four-momentum on constant-time slices, with physical content reduced to a residual causal charge inferred from curvature response.
AI.conclusion: The lightcone singularity in the reduced Yang-Mills stress-energy tensor can be consistently interpreted as a source via a lightcone completion, which is unique up to one parameter χ. The resulting source carries no net four-momentum but encodes a causal charge.

title: Global analysis of a minimally extended scotogenic model
summary: We perform a global analysis of a minimally extended scotogenic model motivated by observed non-zero neutrino masses, viable dark matter (DM) candidates, and the instability of the Standard Model (SM) vacuum at high-energies. We examine the bounded-from-below conditions, vacuum stability, and RG-driven perturbativity bounds arising from the extended scalar sector, alongside a comprehensive set of flavor and electroweak (EW) precision observables - including the muon anomalous magnetic moment $Δa_μ$, the radiative decays $\ell_α \rightarrow \ell_β γ$ and $\ell_α \rightarrow 3\ell_β$, and the $μ\rightarrow e$ conversion rate, the oblique parameters, and leptonic decays of $Z$ and $H$ bosons. A numerical scan reveals four notable features: the DESI BAO bound would rule out the inverted hierarchy if confirmed by other experiments; the oblique parameters are projected to be within the reach of future precision measurements; the viable fermionic DM candidate mass lies in the range $120-350 \func{GeV}$, while the CP-odd scalar is constrained to $350-600 \func{GeV}$; and our result on $Z \rightarrow \func{Invisible}$ is compatible with the world average at the $3σ$ level and is favored by the recent ATLAS measurement at the $3σ$ level.

AI.tldr: This paper globally analyzes a scotogenic model extension addressing neutrino masses, dark matter, and SM vacuum instability, finding that the DESI BAO bound could rule out inverted neutrino hierarchy, oblique parameters are within reach of future precision, viable fermionic DM mass is 120-350 GeV, CP-odd scalar is 350-600 GeV, and Z→Invisible results are compatible with world average at 3σ and favored by ATLAS at 3σ.
AI.motivation: To address three interconnected problems: observed non-zero neutrino masses, viable dark matter candidates, and the instability of the Standard Model vacuum at high energies.
AI.method: Global numerical scan of a minimally extended scotogenic model, analyzing bounded-from-below conditions, vacuum stability, RG-driven perturbativity bounds, and a comprehensive set of flavor and electroweak precision observables including Δa_μ, radiative decays ℓ_α→ℓ_βγ and ℓ_α→3ℓ_β, μ→e conversion, oblique parameters, and leptonic Z and H boson decays.
AI.result: Four key findings: DESI BAO bound could rule out inverted neutrino hierarchy; oblique parameters within reach of future precision measurements; viable fermionic DM mass 120-350 GeV; CP-odd scalar mass 350-600 GeV; Z→Invisible compatible with world average at 3σ and favored by ATLAS at 3σ.
AI.conclusion: The scotogenic model provides a viable framework addressing neutrino masses, DM, and vacuum instability simultaneously, with specific testable predictions for future experiments.

title: Universal Lichnerowicz Lifting of Near-Horizon Soft Modes
summary: A remarkable universality appears in the low-temperature quantum thermodynamics of near-extremal black holes, where distinct parent geometries often lead to the same logarithmic temperature dependence at one loop. In this work, we study the Lichnerowicz spectral origin of this infrared universality and understand why the relevant spectral data become insensitive to the details of the parent geometry. For extremal near-horizon geometries containing a two-dimensional maximally symmetric throat, we construct the normalizable transverse-traceless tensor zero modes associated with near-horizon reparametrizations. Turning on a small temperature lifts these zero modes through the first-order deformation of the Lichnerowicz operator. Although the local matrix element depends on detailed parent-geometry data, these data cancel after projection onto normalized tensor modes, leaving the universal result. For static spherically symmetric backgrounds, the eigenvalue shift is universally proportional to the Fourier mode number and temperature, and the same structure persists for rotating backgrounds, where angular warp factors only modify the overall projection factor. We further show that this lifted bulk spectrum is the Lichnerowicz realization of the Schwarzian soft sector. Thus, the universal first-order result is traced to an infrared bulk-boundary matching between near-horizon tensor zero modes and boundary reparametrization dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper explains the universality of logarithmic temperature dependence in near-extremal black hole thermodynamics by tracing it to Lichnerowicz spectral zero modes lifted by temperature; the universality arises from cancellation of parent-geometry details upon projection, and the lifted spectrum matches the Schwarzian soft sector via bulk-boundary correspondence.
AI.motivation: To understand why distinct parent black hole geometries yield the same universal logarithmic low-temperature corrections in quantum thermodynamics, by investigating the spectral origin of this universality in the Lichnerowicz operator.
AI.method: Construct normalizable transverse-traceless tensor zero modes associated with near-horizon reparametrizations for extremal near-horizon geometries with a 2D maximally symmetric throat; compute first-order eigenvalue shifts from temperature-induced deformation of the Lichnerowicz operator; project onto normalized modes to show cancellation of parent-geometry details.
AI.result: For static spherically symmetric backgrounds, the eigenvalue shift is universally proportional to Fourier mode number and temperature; for rotating backgrounds, angular warp factors modify only the overall projection factor. The lifted bulk spectrum is identified as the Lichnerowicz realization of the Schwarzian soft sector.
AI.conclusion: The universal first-order result originates from infrared bulk-boundary matching between near-horizon tensor zero modes and boundary reparametrization dynamics, explaining the one-loop logarithmic universality in near-extremal black hole thermodynamics.

title: Magnetic moments of decuplet baryons in isospin asymmetric magnetized strange matter
summary: We investigate the in-medium masses and magnetic moments of decuplet baryons $(Δ,Σ^*,Ξ^*,Ω^-)$ in isospin asymmetric magnetized strange matter at finite temperature within a unified chiral effective framework. Medium modifications of baryons are implemented using the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model, where constituent quarks interact via scalar ($σ$, $ζ$, $δ$) and vector ($ω$, $ρ$, $φ$) meson fields considering the Dirac sea effects. The external magnetic field is incorporated through Landau quantization of charged particles together with anomalous magnetic moments (AMM) of baryons. The resulting in-medium mass of constituent quarks and decuplet baryons obtained from the CQMF model are subsequently employed as input to the chiral constituent quark model ($χ$CQM) to evaluate magnetic moments of baryons. Contributions from valence quarks, sea quark spin polarizations, and orbital angular momentum of the quark sea are taken into account. Our results provide a systematic understanding of how dense, hot, and magnetized environments influence the magnetic properties of decuplet baryons.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how dense, hot, and magnetized environments affect the masses and magnetic moments of decuplet baryons (Δ, Σ*, Ξ*, Ω⁻) using a chiral effective framework that combines the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model and the chiral constituent quark model (χCQM), incorporating Dirac sea effects, Landau quantization, and anomalous magnetic moments.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand how isospin asymmetric magnetized strange matter at finite temperature influences the in-medium properties (masses and magnetic moments) of decuplet baryons, which is relevant for astrophysical environments like neutron stars and heavy-ion collisions.
AI.method: The chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model is used to compute in-medium masses of constituent quarks and decuplet baryons, incorporating scalar (σ, ζ, δ) and vector (ω, ρ, φ) meson fields with Dirac sea effects. External magnetic field is included via Landau quantization and anomalous magnetic moments (AMM). These results feed into the chiral constituent quark model (χCQM) to evaluate magnetic moments, accounting for valence quarks, sea quark spin polarizations, and orbital angular momentum of the quark sea.
AI.result: The results provide a systematic understanding of how dense, hot, and magnetized environments modify the magnetic properties of decuplet baryons.
AI.conclusion: The unified chiral effective framework successfully captures the combined effects of temperature, density, isospin asymmetry, and magnetic fields on decuplet baryon properties, offering insights for astrophysical and heavy-ion collision contexts.

title: Laplace Space for Cosmological Correlators
summary: Deep inside the horizon, every cosmological mode oscillates as a flat-space plane wave. A Laplace transform turns this fact into a general method: it resolves each curved-space mode into a superposition of plane waves dressed by a kernel that encodes the spacetime geometry, field content and dynamics, collapsing the time integrals onto flat-space ones. This provides simple diagrammatic rules that turn cosmological correlator diagrams into their flat-space counterparts integrated against Laplace-space kernels. On the paradigmatic massive single exchange, this integral representation makes the energy singularities manifest and evaluates in closed form as a single, rapidly convergent series valid throughout the kinematic domain, with no patching of separate expansions. The Laplace approach sheds conceptual and computational light on cosmological correlators in virtually any theory of the early universe.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a Laplace transform method that maps curved-space cosmological correlators onto flat-space plane wave superpositions, enabling closed-form series evaluations (e.g., massive single exchange) without patching separate expansions.
AI.motivation: Cosmological correlators in curved spacetime are difficult to compute analytically, often requiring piecewise expansions; the authors seek a general, unified method that simplifies these calculations.
AI.method: A Laplace transform resolves each curved-space mode into a superposition of flat-space plane waves via a kernel encoding geometry, field content, and dynamics. This collapses time integrals onto flat-space ones, providing diagrammatic rules to convert cosmological correlator diagrams into flat-space counterparts integrated against Laplace-space kernels.
AI.result: On the massive single exchange, the method yields a closed-form, single rapidly convergent series valid throughout the kinematic domain, with no patching required. Energy singularities become manifest.
AI.conclusion: The Laplace approach provides conceptual and computational clarity for cosmological correlators in virtually any early-universe theory, unifying curved-space computations via flat-space techniques.

title: Stochastic gravitational wave spectrum from cosmic string emitting gauge bosons and Majorana fermions
summary: The effect of particle radiation on the spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) from cosmic strings is studied. We consider cosmic strings in an Abelian-Higgs model coupling with Majorana fermion whose mass is generated by the Higgs field, motivated by a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, in which the Majorana fermions are identified with right-handed neutrinos. Taking the energy loss by particle radiation into account, we evaluate the resultant SGWB spectrum and demonstrate the emergence of very high frequency cutoff due to the particle radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how particle radiation from cosmic strings in an Abelian-Higgs model with Majorana fermions (motivated by a gauged U(1)_{B-L} model) affects the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) spectrum, finding that particle radiation introduces a very high frequency cutoff.
AI.motivation: To investigate the effect of particle radiation on the SGWB from cosmic strings, motivated by a gauged U(1)_{B-L} model where Majorana fermions (right-handed neutrinos) couple to the Higgs field.
AI.method: The authors consider cosmic strings in an Abelian-Higgs model coupled with Majorana fermions whose mass is generated by the Higgs field. They incorporate energy loss from particle radiation into the calculation of the SGWB spectrum.
AI.result: The SGWB spectrum exhibits a very high frequency cutoff due to particle radiation from cosmic strings.
AI.conclusion: Particle radiation significantly modifies the SGWB spectrum by introducing a high-frequency cutoff, which has implications for detectability of SGWB from cosmic strings.

title: Massive Cosmological Correlators from Flat Space: a Laplace-Space Approach
summary: We develop a new approach to cosmological correlators, built on a simple physical fact: deep inside the Hubble radius every mode oscillates as a flat-space plane wave, the curvature of spacetime making itself felt only as the mode is stretched towards the horizon. A Laplace transform turns this observation into a computational tool, resolving each curved-space mode function into a continuous superposition of plane waves labelled by a dual variable and dressed by a kernel that encodes the spacetime geometry, field content and dynamics. Every time integral then reduces to an elementary flat-space one, yielding simple diagrammatic rules for cosmological correlators. We illustrate the construction on the massive single-exchange correlator. The Laplace representation makes its total- and partial-energy singularities transparent ''from flat space'', and yields a single closed-form, rapidly convergent series valid throughout the entire kinematic domain. Although developed for conformally coupled fields exchanging massive scalars in de Sitter, the approach carries over essentially unchanged to virtually all situations of interest in primordial cosmology.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a Laplace transform-based approach that reduces curved-space cosmological correlator computations to flat-space plane wave calculations, demonstrated on the massive single-exchange correlator.
AI.motivation: To overcome the computational complexity of cosmological correlators in curved spacetime by leveraging the physical insight that modes oscillate as flat-space plane waves deep inside the Hubble radius.
AI.method: A Laplace transform decomposes curved-space mode functions into continuous superpositions of flat-space plane waves, with a kernel encoding geometry, field content, and dynamics; every time integral then reduces to an elementary flat-space integral.
AI.result: The approach yields simple diagrammatic rules for cosmological correlators; the massive single-exchange correlator is computed in closed form as a rapidly convergent series valid across the entire kinematic domain, with transparent total- and partial-energy singularities.
AI.conclusion: Although developed for conformally coupled fields with massive scalars in de Sitter, the method generalizes to virtually all relevant primordial cosmology scenarios.

title: Thermodynamical analysis of QGP using effective PNJL model with Quasiparticle approach
summary: We study the thermodynamics of the quark-gluon plasma using an effective Two flavor Polyakov Nambu Jona Lasinio (PNJL) model extended by a quasiparticle description for quarks and gluons, incorporating temperature dependent quark masses within the PNJL framework. Two variants, Quasiparticle Model-I and Quasiparticle Model-II, are implemented to investigate bulk thermodynamic observables such as pressure, energy density, entropy density, specific heat, and the speed of sound. The combined framework yields a robust baseline for the description of hot QGP dynamics in the high temperature regime at vanishing chemical potential and zero magnetic field. Systematic comparison with lattice QCD results shows an excellent agreement and clear improvement over conventional PNJL implementations. We observe that both variants complement each other, offering mutually consistent insight into quasiparticle mass effects and medium response in the deconfined phase. This mutual consistency validates the physical foundation of the overall quasiparticle mechanism, reinforcing the credibility of the calculated Equation of State. Finally, the quasiparticle model extension improves PNJL from a descriptive tool to a more qualitative phenomenological approach, enabling an improved description of the strong interacting quark-gluon plasma.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the PNJL model with quasiparticle descriptions (two variants: QPM-I and QPM-II) incorporating temperature-dependent quark masses to study QGP thermodynamics. Both variants show excellent agreement with lattice QCD results and improve upon conventional PNJL, providing a robust EoS for hot QGP at zero chemical potential and magnetic field.
AI.motivation: To improve the conventional PNJL model's descriptive capability for QGP thermodynamics by incorporating quasiparticle effects (temperature-dependent masses) to better match lattice QCD results and transition from a descriptive to a more qualitative phenomenological tool.
AI.method: Two quasiparticle variants (QPM-I and QPM-II) are implemented within the PNJL framework, introducing temperature-dependent quark masses. Bulk thermodynamic observables (pressure, energy density, entropy density, specific heat, speed of sound) are computed at vanishing chemical potential and zero magnetic field, then systematically compared with lattice QCD data.
AI.result: Excellent agreement with lattice QCD results and clear improvement over conventional PNJL. Both variants complement each other, providing mutually consistent insights into quasiparticle mass effects and medium response in the deconfined phase.
AI.conclusion: The quasiparticle extension elevates PNJL from a descriptive tool to a qualitative phenomenological approach, enabling an improved description of strongly interacting QGP. The mutual consistency between variants validates the physical foundation of the quasiparticle mechanism and the credibility of the calculated Equation of State.

title: The IKKT renormalization group flow is IIB: toward zero-d holography
summary: Supergravity solutions describing stacks of D$p$-branes with $p\neq 3$ feature a non-constant dilaton profile, which is holographically mapped to the running of the SYM coupling in $(p+1)$ dimensions. For D-instantons ($p=-1$), the lack of space and time in the IKKT matrix model makes such an interpretation difficult at first. In this letter, we propose a method to achieve this based on two closely related concepts: the IKKT method of integrating out heavy strings in a Coulomb branch vacuum and the matrix RG flow of Brézin and Zinn-Justin (BZJ). The notable difference between the two is that the BZJ RG flow also integrates over the Coulomb branch position. We first apply the Coulomb branch method and by relating the coefficient of the leading correction to the IKKT action with the string coupling, we can compute its dependence on the Coulomb branch position, finding a match between matrix theory and supergravity. Next, we apply the BZJ-flow to the IKKT partition function, which leads to a running of the coupling constant $g$ with the rank $N$ of the matrix model, reproducing the $N$-dependence of the axio-dilaton field in supergravity.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a holographic interpretation for D-instantons (p=-1) by connecting the IKKT matrix model's coupling running with supergravity's axio-dilaton profile, using two complementary methods: the Coulomb branch integration of heavy strings and the Brézin-Zinn-Justin matrix RG flow.
AI.motivation: For Dp-branes with p≠3, the non-constant dilaton in supergravity maps to running SYM coupling in holography. However, for D-instantons (p=-1) in the IKKT matrix model, the lack of spacetime dimensions makes this holographic interpretation unclear. The paper aims to resolve this puzzle.
AI.method: Two methods are used: (1) The Coulomb branch method, where heavy strings are integrated out in a Coulomb branch vacuum, relating the leading correction coefficient to the string coupling and computing its dependence on the Coulomb branch position. (2) The Brézin-Zinn-Justin (BZJ) RG flow applied to the IKKT partition function, which integrates over the Coulomb branch position and yields a running coupling constant g with matrix rank N.
AI.result: The Coulomb branch method yields agreement between matrix theory and supergravity for the string coupling's dependence on the Coulomb branch position. The BZJ flow reproduces the N-dependence of the axio-dilaton field in supergravity through the running of g with N.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methods successfully establish a holographic interpretation for D-instantons, demonstrating that the IKKT matrix model can capture supergravity's axio-dilaton dynamics through either the Coulomb branch or the BZJ RG flow.

title: Hard-Region Fermion Self-Energy and Fermion--Photon Vertex in Thermal QED through Two Loops
comment: 36 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables; ancillary Mathematica notebook included
summary: In massless thermal QED in a general covariant $R_ξ$ gauge, we compute hard-region contributions to the fermion self-energy and the off-shell fermion--photon vertex at one-loop next-to-leading power and two-loop leading power in the soft-momentum expansion. The zero-temperature counterterms are also included to renormalize these hard amplitudes. Chiral invariance restricts the off-shell two-fermion--$N$-photon vertex to vector ($γ_μ$) and axial-vector ($γ_μγ_5$) Dirac structures. The vector part is constrained by the Ward--Takahashi identity (WTI), while the axial part is transverse to the photon momentum. The symmetries and hermiticity of the theory impose definite constraints -- including reality, momentum reversal, and fermion-leg exchange properties -- which lead to selection rules in the soft expansion: a contribution at power $r$ can be nonzero only when $r+N+1$ is even, with $N=0$ for the self-energy. At the integrand level, we decompose the amplitudes into independent statistical and gauge sectors, and verify the WTI and axial transversality sector by sector. Notably, the gauge-dependent sectors split into mixed metric--longitudinal and fully longitudinal sectors at two loops. The latter vanishes at leading power and reappears at next-to-leading power while satisfying the constraints. We show that these hard-region self-energy corrections do not generate a finite contribution to the fermion damping rate. These results provide hard-region input for mass shifts and inclusive rates, as well as for the construction of the next-to-leading-order fermionic effective Lagrangian.

The hard-region self-energy corrections are shown not to contribute to the fermion damping rate.

Decomposes amplitudes into independent statistical and gauge sectors, verifying Ward-Takahashi identity and axial transversality sector by sector.

title: Probing Probability Geometry with Schwinger--Dyson Identities: Score Mismatch, Fisher Information, and Configurational Temperature
summary: We develop a geometric interpretation of Schwinger--Dyson identities by showing that their violations are controlled by a single score-mismatch field $δs$. For an arbitrary sampled probability distribution $Q$ and equilibrium measure $P_{\rm eq}$, every Schwinger--Dyson violation is determined by $δs = \nabla \log (Q / P_{\rm eq})$, which characterizes the departure from equilibrium. Each Schwinger--Dyson identity measures a projection of this field onto a probe direction in configuration space. The relative Fisher information is its squared norm. This gives a universal bound relating Fisher information to the complete Schwinger--Dyson hierarchy, thus implying that convergence in Fisher information restores all Schwinger--Dyson identities. We further obtain a variational characterization of the relative Fisher information in terms of Schwinger--Dyson violations, leading to a natural tomographic interpretation in which increasingly rich families of probe fields encode progressively more information about the underlying probability distortion. The configurational temperature, within this framework, emerges as a distinguished Schwinger--Dyson probe. The Stein operators and score-function methods arise naturally from the same probability-geometric structure. The score-mismatch field, therefore, provides a unified geometric language for understanding Schwinger--Dyson identities, configurational temperature, Fisher information, and non-equilibrium sampling in stochastic processes.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework where Schwinger-Dyson identity violations are governed by a score-mismatch field δs = ∇ log(Q/P_eq), linking it to Fisher information, configurational temperature, and non-equilibrium sampling.
AI.motivation: To develop a unified geometric interpretation of Schwinger-Dyson identities and their violations, bridging probability theory, statistical mechanics, and stochastic sampling.
AI.method: Geometric analysis showing that Schwinger-Dyson violations are controlled by the score-mismatch field δs = ∇ log(Q/P_eq), deriving bounds relating Fisher information to the Schwinger-Dyson hierarchy, and establishing a variational characterization of relative Fisher information.
AI.result: Relative Fisher information equals the squared norm of the score-mismatch field; convergence in Fisher information restores all Schwinger-Dyson identities; configurational temperature emerges as a distinguished probe; Stein operators and score-function methods naturally arise from the same geometric structure.
AI.conclusion: The score-mismatch field provides a unified geometric language for Schwinger-Dyson identities, configurational temperature, Fisher information, and non-equilibrium sampling.

title: StringSpinner 2.0: Enabling quark spin effects in PYTHIA for $e^+e^-$ annihilation
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, to be submitted to Computer Physics Communications
summary: The StringSpinner package, which implements quark spin effects in the PYTHIA event generator using the string+${}^3P_0$ model of hadronization, is extended to handle the process $e^+e^-\rightarrow q\bar{q} \rightarrow hadrons$ at leading order. The correlations between the spin states of the $q\bar{q}$ pair produced in the reaction are described by a joint spin density matrix. The spin correlations are propagated along the string fragmentation chain by using the rules of the string+${}^3P_0$ model and are implemented for the production of pseudoscalar and vector mesons. The new version of the package can be used to simulate spin effects in $e^+e^-$ annihilation like the Collins and the Artru-Collins asymmetries. It can also be applied to the study of other spin effects in hadronization predicted by the string+${}^3P_0$ model with a user-defined joint spin density matrix of the $q\bar{q}$ pair. To showcase the usage of the package the polar angle dependence of the Collins asymmetries for back-to-back pions is studied and compared with the available data.

AI.tldr: The StringSpinner package is extended to simulate quark spin effects in e+e- → qq̅ → hadrons, implementing spin correlations from the string+³P₀ hadronization model for pseudoscalar and vector mesons, and enabling studies of Collins and Artru-Collins asymmetries.
AI.motivation: To extend the StringSpinner package (originally for DIS) to e+e- annihilation, enabling simulation of spin-dependent hadronization effects like Collins asymmetries in this important production channel.
AI.method: Extends StringSpinner to leading-order e+e- → qq̅ → hadrons using a joint spin density matrix for the qq̅ pair, propagating spin correlations via string+³P₀ model rules, implemented for pseudoscalar and vector meson production.

title: The Effect of Topological Defects and Magnetic Flux on Fully-Heavy Tetraquarks and Mass Spectra of Heavy Quarkonia Using the Analytical Exact Iteration Method
summary: Investigating the non-perturbative behavior of QCD and the dynamics of strong interaction is crucial for the study of heavy quarkonia and the understanding of exotic fully-heavy tetraquarks. In this work, using the analytical exact iteration method (AEIM), the analytical eigenvalue solutions of the non-relativistic Schrödinger equation are obtained in the presence of topological defects and external magnetic flux. The interactions are modelled using a modified Cornell potential supplemented by harmonic and inverse quadratic terms. We demonstrate that the energy levels are distinctly shifted by the topological defect parameter ($α$). The mass spectra of heavy quarkonia ($c\bar{c}$ and $b\bar{b}$) and fully-heavy tetraquarks ($cc\bar{c}\bar{c}$ and $bb\bar{b}\bar{b}$) across several radial and orbital excitation states are successfully calculated using this approach. The computed masses of bottomonium and charmonium accord well with current theoretical predictions and experimental findings. Our findings for the heavy tetraquarks are in line with previous theoretical investigations that consider tetraquarks as configurations of diquarks and antidiquarks. The numerical results demonstrate that a nontrivial interaction between the confining potential and the background space-time geometry governs the mass hierarchy of these exotic hadronic states, providing high-precision data with excellent agreement with established theoretical models and experimental benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Using the analytical exact iteration method (AEIM), this work solves the Schrödinger equation with a modified Cornell potential in topological defect backgrounds and magnetic flux, calculating mass spectra for heavy quarkonia (c\bar{c}, b\bar{b}) and fully-heavy tetraquarks (cc\bar{c}\bar{c}, bb\bar{b}\bar{b}) that agree well with experimental and theoretical benchmarks.
AI.motivation: To understand non-perturbative QCD behavior and strong interaction dynamics for studying heavy quarkonia and exotic fully-heavy tetraquarks, particularly how topological defects and external magnetic fields affect their mass spectra.
AI.method: The analytical exact iteration method (AEIM) is applied to solve the non-relativistic Schrödinger equation with a modified Cornell potential (including harmonic and inverse quadratic terms) in the presence of topological defects and external magnetic flux.
AI.result: Energy levels are distinctly shifted by the topological defect parameter α. Calculated masses for bottomonium and charmonium match current theoretical predictions and experimental findings. Tetraquark masses align with previous diquark-antidiquark configuration studies. A nontrivial interaction between the confining potential and background space-time geometry governs the mass hierarchy.
AI.conclusion: The AEIM approach provides high-precision data with excellent agreement with established theoretical models and experimental benchmarks, demonstrating that topological defects and magnetic flux significantly influence heavy quarkonium and tetraquark mass spectra.
